source_receipts.location: Abstract and performance-evaluation methods: same-location 10-fold and between-location validation; abrupt-condition failures.
source_receipts.finding: The paper reports improved calibration under its evaluated splits but identifies failures after abrupt environmental changes.

source_receipts.location: data.zip: timestamped sagatea-111, tanashi-117, and tanashi-118 CSV files; verified MD5.
source_receipts.finding: The official data contain hourly reference temperature and environmental covariates at three sites over the reported observation period.

source_receipts.location: cv.r lines 43–70: random within-location fold assignment and linear/ANN fitting.
source_receipts.finding: The published within-location workflow samples row-level folds at random, whereas the raw data permit contiguous temporal evaluation.

question: For a fixed site, does the published calibration retain its reported advantage when trained on earlier contiguous observations and tested on later observations across an abrupt-condition boundary?
fragility: Randomly interleaved within-site folds can leak temporally adjacent environmental states into both training and test data.
alternative_explanation: The reported improvement may reflect interpolation among nearby conditions rather than calibration transfer through an abrupt solar-radiation or rainfall shift.
independent_check: Predeclare one chronological split per site and the same published covariates/model settings; train only before each split, test only after it, then compare temporal-held-out MAE with the published random-fold MAE and with the linear baseline.

outcomes.positive: Stable temporal-held-out improvement supports the narrow claim that the calibration transfers across later conditions at those sites.
outcomes.null: Loss of precision or no improvement means random-fold success does not establish temporal transfer.
outcomes.contrary: Worse post-boundary performance than the uncalibrated or linear baseline would challenge the claimed practical calibration advantage.

material_mismatch: Three Japanese sensor sites and the recorded 305-day period do not represent every climate, device, or long-term sensor-drift regime; the result would be site-period specific.
plain_language_verdict: INTERVIEW-READY CANDIDATE — this is a reproducible test of time-ordered calibration transfer within the supplied sensor data. It does not assert that the method works or fails universally, and it is not yet a selected target or System-2 input.
next_permitted_action: Form the exactly-three-packet first-interview batch using packets 1–3, with no candidate promoted until that gate issues a documented disposition.
